introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2019. Time allowed: two and a half hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (One hour, "Answer all Questions"): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (30 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (1 hour): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
incertitudes: Question 9 : le sujet n'imprime pas de total ; les marques par bloc donnent 4 + (3 + 3) + (2 + 3) = 15 (identique aux autres options, qui portent « Total 15 marks »). `points` de l'exercice laissé vide ; ceux des sous-questions : a = 4, b = 6 (3 + 3), c = 5 (2 + 3). Les schémas demandés en (a) sont à tracer par le candidat et sont décrits.

Question 9(c)(i) : « physical quantities that can be varied ... using a mobile phone » est lu comme la capacité C et l'inductance L du circuit d'accord (donc la fréquence accordée) ; la formulation du sujet est ambiguë.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the diagram of a simple radio receiver. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate).** A block diagram, from left to right, with arrows showing the signal path:

**aerial (antenna)** $\rightarrow$ **tuning circuit** (an inductor $L$ in parallel with a variable capacitor $C$, selects the wanted carrier frequency, the unwanted stations are rejected) $\rightarrow$ **radio-frequency (RF) amplifier** $\rightarrow$ **demodulator (detector)** (a diode with a smoothing capacitor, which removes the carrier and recovers the audio signal) $\rightarrow$ **audio-frequency (AF) amplifier** $\rightarrow$ **loudspeaker** (or earphone).

The tuning circuit is also connected to the **earth** on its lower side. Label each block and the signal in it: weak modulated carrier from the aerial, selected carrier, amplified carrier, audio signal after the detector, amplified audio signal.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Briefly explain the difference between FM and AM transmission. *[3 marks]*

(ii) A tuning circuit contains an inductor of inductance $12.7\ \mathrm{mH}$. If a capacitor of capacitance $2.00\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ is connected to the circuit, calculate the frequency to which the circuit is tuned. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** In both systems a high-frequency **carrier wave** is **modulated** by the audio signal.

- In **amplitude modulation (AM)**, the **amplitude** of the carrier varies in step with the audio signal, while the carrier frequency stays constant. AM is simple and has a long range, but it is sensitive to electrical noise (noise changes the amplitude), so the quality is lower.
- In **frequency modulation (FM)**, the **frequency** of the carrier varies in step with the audio signal (the frequency deviation is proportional to the amplitude of the signal), while the carrier amplitude stays constant. FM is almost free of noise (which mostly affects amplitude) and gives better sound quality, but it needs a wider bandwidth and has a shorter range.

**(ii)** The resonant (tuned) frequency of an LC circuit is
$$f = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}} = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{12.7\times10^{-3}\times2.00\times10^{-6}}} = \frac{1}{2\pi\times1.594\times10^{-4}} = 9.99\times10^{2}\ \mathrm{Hz}$$

**The circuit is tuned to a frequency of about $1.00\times10^{3}\ \mathrm{Hz}$ ($1.0\ \mathrm{kHz}$).**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State two physical quantities that can be varied in order to capture a particular radio station using a mobile phone. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State and explain two uses of cell phones. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** A radio station is selected by **tuning the receiver to its carrier frequency**, that is, by varying the **capacitance $C$** and/or the **inductance $L$** of the tuning circuit, so that its resonant frequency $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$ equals the frequency of the wanted station. (In a phone, a digital tuner changes this effective $L$ or $C$ electronically; the quantity set by the user is the **frequency** (wavelength) of the station.)

**(ii)** Two uses of cell phones (any two, each with its explanation):

1. **Voice and text communication** (calls and SMS): the phone sends and receives microwave signals to and from the nearest base station, so people can communicate from almost anywhere.
2. **Internet access and mobile services** (e-mail, social media, mobile money payments such as those used in Cameroon): the phone connects through the cellular data network (3G/4G) to the internet and exchanges digital data with servers, so information and services are available without a fixed line.
